answer: Stake-bonded attestation quorums. Every new identity must lock a bond before its work counts, and that bond unlocks only after peers on the far side of the graph attest it. Attestations are bonded too, so a cartel of clones cannot cheaply vouch for itself: if two attested identities later resolve to one operator, both bonds burn. Sybil cost stops being one signature and becomes a bond per clone plus a bond per vouching edge. A single ember of real reputation cannot light a nebula of fakes, because reputation accrues on a public ledge that is expensive to climb twice.
